interface.title: LabBridge
interface.field: Laboratory data management / bioassay QC (96-well plate-reader immunoassay data, e.g. IL6 concentrations)
interface.stage_of_work: Data intake and quality control right after acquisition, before downstream analysis or ML modelling
interface.what_it_is_for: A six-step Streamlit wizard that takes a messy plate-reader export, maps its columns to a standard schema with a person checking the choices, flags bad wells on a plate heatmap, runs scientific QC (standard curve, replicate CV, Levey-Jennings/Westgard control monitoring), gives a PASS/REVIEW/FAIL fitness verdict, and exports the cleaned dataset with a quality summary and transformation log.

data.note: First pass: uploaded messy_plate_long.csv through the file uploader (97 rows × 12 columns, detected as long format). Later passes used the 'Load sample plate export' button, which loads the same messy_plate_long.csv. The app reads the control-run history for the Levey-Jennings tab (24 runs) by itself.

tree.general: Turn a raw instrument export into a standardized, quality-checked dataset with a documented verdict on whether it is fit to analyse
tree.specific: Take messy_plate_long.csv through LabBridge's six steps (Upload → Schema mapping → Data QC → QC Intelligence → Clean preview → Export) and download the cleaned CSV, the quality summary and the transformation log

features.name: Column-to-schema mapper with confidence scores
features.general: Match each column of an incoming table to a fixed set of standard fields, show how confident each match is and why, and let a person confirm, change or drop each match before processing
features.specific: Schema mapping step: each raw column (Plate, Conc., Anlyst…) gets a proposed canonical field, a green/yellow/red status, a % confidence bar, a reason ('known synonym', 'fuzzy match', 'values look like'), and a 'Your decision' dropdown that includes '— leave unmapped —'. A yellow banner names the columns that need judgement. Confirm runs QC; manual choices later show up only as counts in the export summary and as rule 'manual' entries in the transformation log
steps: Read the proposed mapping, confidence and reason for each raw column
Open the decision dropdown on a yellow (needs review) column
Pick a different canonical field or '— leave unmapped —'
Press Confirm mapping & run quality checks
See the choice recorded in the summary counts (auto/manual/unmapped) and in the transformation log
serves_tasks: Review proposed column matches with their confidence and fix the uncertain ones

features.name: Plate heatmap with linked flag table
features.general: Show every position of a sample grid coloured by its reading, mark the problem positions, and list each problem next to it with a severity, a type and a reason
features.specific: Data QC step: 8×12 plate map coloured by log reading (viridis) with ▲ on flagged wells and blanks for missing/overflow wells, hover tooltips for row/column, next to a 'Flagged wells' table (severity error/warn, well, flag code, reason). Headline numbers (rows, flags, errors, warnings, ML-ready) and a 'What these flags mean' glossary go with them
steps: Scan the plate map for ▲ markers and empty (white) wells
Hover a well to get its row and column
Find that well in the Flagged wells table and scroll sideways to read the reason
Open 'What these flags mean' to look up a flag code
serves_tasks: See where problem wells sit on the plate and why each was flagged

features.name: Standard-curve fit with back-calculated concentrations
features.general: Fit a calibration line through reference samples, check it against an acceptance threshold, and convert unknown readings to concentrations with 95% confidence intervals and an in-range check
features.specific: Standard curve tab: R², slope, number of standard levels and PASS/FAIL acceptance (R² ≥ 0.98); scatter of measured signal vs expected nM with the fitted line and hover tooltips per standard well; a sortable table of samples with calc_conc_nM, ci95_low, ci95_high, in_curve_range
steps: Read the fit numbers and acceptance verdict
Hover a standard point to see its well, expected and measured value
Sort the quantified-sample table by calculated concentration
Check the CI bounds and the in_curve_range tick for each sample
serves_tasks: Fit a calibration curve and back-calculate unknown concentrations with confidence intervals

features.name: Replicate CV reliability chart
features.general: Rank each sample by how much its repeat measurements disagree, against a fixed limit, and colour each as good, watch or fail
features.specific: Replicate reliability tab: horizontal bar chart of replicate CV% per sample_id with a dashed 25% limit line and good/watch/fail colouring; tooltip gives n_reps, mean, cv_pct and reliability; a headline counts failing samples
steps: Read the headline count of samples over the CV limit
Find red bars past the dashed 25% line
Hover a bar to read n_reps, mean and CV%

features.name: Levey-Jennings control chart with Westgard rules
features.general: Plot a control measurement run by run against limits from a baseline, and mark the runs that break standard rules for drift or shift
features.specific: Control monitoring tab: positive-control value (nM) by run # with the mean line and ±2SD/±3SD dashed limits from the validated baseline; violating runs drawn as red triangles; tooltip gives run_id, value, z-score and Westgard flags (e.g. 1_3s;2_2s); headline gives the baseline mean/SD and the number of violations
steps: Read the baseline mean/SD and the number of violations
Look for points beyond the 2SD/3SD lines or trending runs
Hover a red triangle to see run_id, z-score and which Westgard rules fired
serves_tasks: Track a control across runs over time and catch drift

features.name: Before/after normalization log with clean-table preview
features.general: List every automatic change made to the data (field, rule, old value, new value) next to the resulting clean table, so nothing changes without being shown
features.specific: Clean preview step: 'Before → after · 178 values normalized' table (well, field, transformation such as NORMALIZED / DECIMAL_NORMALIZED / EMBEDDED_UNIT_STRIPPED / UNIT_NORMALIZED / DATE_NORMALIZED, before, after) with a 'Show all normalizations' toggle, followed by the clean dataset in canonical columns with a qc_flag for each row, searchable from the table toolbar
steps: Turn on 'Show all normalizations' to list every change
Scroll through the transformation types
Search the clean table for a flag (e.g. 'SAT') to jump to that row
Check that flagged rows carry their qc_flag
serves_tasks: Inspect every automatic correction and the cleaned table

features.name: Audited export bundle
features.general: Package the cleaned data, a readable quality summary and a machine-readable log of every change for download together
features.specific: Export step: three download buttons (Clean dataset CSV, Quality summary Markdown, Transformation log JSON), with a rendered data-quality summary (rows in/out, column mapping counts, required fields present, normalizations, flags by type, ML-ready YES/NO) and the first rows of the audit trail shown on the page
steps: Read the rendered data-quality summary and ML-ready status
Look over the transformation log preview
Download the clean CSV, the Markdown summary and the JSON log
serves_tasks: Download the cleaned dataset, a quality report and a full log of changes

features.name: Fitness verdict summary
features.general: Combine the results of several independent quality checks (calibration acceptance, replicate agreement, statistical outliers, control-rule violations) into one go/no-go banner, with a severity-marked reason for each check
features.specific: Fitness verdict tab: a single PASS/REVIEW/FAIL banner (seen here only as '⛔ FAIL — Not fit for analysis yet') above one reason line per check, each with a severity icon: curve passed (R²=1.000), 2 replicate failures, 2 outliers, control drift (1_3s, 2_2s)
steps: Read the verdict banner
Read each per-check reason and its severity icon
Open the tab behind a failing reason (e.g. Replicate reliability or Control monitoring) to see the detail
serves_tasks: Get an overall go/no-go verdict on whether the dataset can be used
